objective: test the frozen rotation wrappers on a sample that never entered any earlier grid, after CP8-A made the existing statistics trustworthy

design.gate: the runner re-derived the content hash, all 120 angles from the seed, the arm labels and the cell arithmetic before scoring anything, and aborts on any mismatch: an independent test is only independent if the sample cannot have moved after the freeze

dataset.name: MPEG-7 CE-Shape-1 (S1)
dataset.archive_sha256_gate: the run refuses to start unless the archive on disk is the build the design was frozen against

gallery.name: mpeg7_full
gallery.why: the whole archive, not the 5-per-class D4 gallery: only 2 of the 24 frozen queries are in that subset, and T0 needs the exact target present. A larger library is the harder test, and no candidate was chosen after seeing a result.

official_toolbox.status: official weights loaded read-only; nothing here modifies them

smoke_run.note: a limited run writes only to checkpoint8/_smoke, so a partial sample can never be read as the promised 24-query table

metric_definitions: Precision@K = hits / min(k, returned); Recall@K = hits / the same-class candidates this query retained, a per-query denominator, undefined when nothing remains
paired differences are published as agreement(B) - agreement(A) under the name second_minus_first, the one convention CP8-A made enforced

coverage_audit.derived_from: the descriptors in queries[]; no query, class or angle was changed by it
coverage_audit.honest_finding: a family whose n_meeting is below n_queries is under-covered: the label describes the design intent, the count states what the frozen draw actually supplies, and a headline for that family may only be read over the queries that pass.
coverage_audit.method: each family's measurable_expectation restated as bounds on circularity, solidity, elongation and hull-gap runs, evaluated per query and counted per family

criteria.why: the concavity of the C or U

curved.if_short_falls_then: a query that fails the axis bound is a ring-like outline; it still tests rotation observability, just not the 'bent' story

forked.if_short_falls_then: branch-heavy outlines are where a single principal axis stops meaning anything; fewer of them weakens the strongest argument against pose search

criteria.why: two lobes fill most of the hull

heart.if_short_falls_then: the heart family is the only one whose label is unambiguous, so it carries the shape-specific claim

criteria.why: protruding parts make several separate gaps

irregular_natural.if_short_falls_then: these are the closest thing to a real silhouette, so a shortfall here is a shortfall in the most transfer-relevant family

criteria.why: isotropic, so rotation is nearly unobservable

near_circle.if_short_falls_then: the isotropic case is the one place a rotation wrapper should be provably worthless; if these queries are not isotropic the study cannot make that claim, only measure the roundish ones that survive

human_perception.status: CP8-C collects no human ratings and therefore adds no independent perceptual evidence. The only perceptual study remains the H1 agreement table, which scores the 250 rated pairs -- a different stimulus set from these 24 MPEG-7 shapes.
human_perception.category_labels_are: a relevance proxy, not a similarity judgement

limits: Independent means **disjoint query instances from the scored cells of this benchmark**, not a different data distribution: gallery and queries are both MPEG-7 CE-Shape-1, so a wrapper that happens to fit this dataset's drawing style still fits.
The 1 400-shape pool was already the *candidate* set in D2/D6, so the queries are new while the gallery is not. Nothing in this round can measure transfer to a pool the arms have never seen.

No new human ratings are collected. The human-perception axis is re-used from H1 with its own provenance, so this study does NOT independently validate perceptual similarity and must not be reported as if it did.
The categories are MPEG-7 object labels. They are a relevance proxy for class retrieval only, never a similarity judgement.

Six arms are scored, not sixteen: the cheapest and the strongest wrapper families are represented (R2/R3 on both networks) plus the three EarthGlyph references, while R0/R1_36/R1_72 and E3/canonical are deliberately absent. A claim about *those* arms cannot come from this file.

The family labels state a design intent; ``coverage_audit`` counts, from the descriptors already in ``queries``, how many frozen draws actually satisfy that intent's geometric criteria. A family below its full count is under-covered, and its headline may only be read over the queries that pass -- loosening a criterion after seeing a shortfall would be result-shopping.

the gallery is the full archive while D6 scored a 5-per-class subset, so a CP8 number is not comparable digit-for-digit with a D6 number -- only the direction and the ranking are quoted across the two
24 queries is the promised sample, not a large one: intervals are clustered by query and stay wide, which is the honest reading rather than a defect

cp8_full_rankings_T2.npz.note: full T2 ranking per (arm, query, pose), so every headline can be recomputed without running an encoder again
